intro: Bolivia, named after Simón Bolívar, is a high Andean country with a large Indigenous population and a silver-mining past.

chapters.title: Tiwanaku
text: Near Lake Titicaca, the Tiwanaku civilisation built a great stone city between about 500 and 1000. Later the region became part of the Inca Empire.

chapters.title: Potosí's silver
text: After the Spanish conquest, silver from the Cerro Rico mountain at Potosí made it one of the largest cities in the world in the 1600s. Enslaved Indigenous and African workers died in huge numbers in the mines.

highlight.title: Rich mountain
highlight.text: 'Vale un Potosí', worth a Potosí, came to mean something priceless.

chapters.title: Independence and after
text: Bolivia became independent in 1825. It lost its coast to Chile in the War of the Pacific and land to Brazil and Paraguay. In 2006 Evo Morales became the first Indigenous president. In 2025 Rodrigo Paz won the presidency, ending nearly 20 years of rule by the MAS party.
